findings.original_assumption: The variables belong to a commutative unital algebra.
findings.finding: The first-excluded-prefix identity uses only finite sums, products, zero and one; a commutative semiring suffices.
findings.proposed_revision: Let R be a commutative semiring, let t belong to R and let (u_x) be a family of elements of R. The same displayed identity holds.
findings.impact: Strengthens generality of article Lemma 5.1. Its application to signed-measure convolution algebras is unchanged. No change to constants, exponents or asymptotic claims.

findings.original_assumption: The original proof uses analytic square-root branches, a Cauchy estimate, a tail bound and a polynomial equality case.
findings.finding: Finite formal-series coefficients and separation of integer squares prove the same uniform bound U <= (64R)^d by an entirely algebraic argument.
findings.proposed_revision: Use D=2^d, A=DP and Q=D^2G-A^2. Formal coefficient cancellation gives degree Q <= k-1 and H(Q) <= (k+1)2^(5d)R^d <= (64R)^d. If Q(U) is nonzero, integer-square separation gives 2^k U^k <= |Q(U)| <= k H(Q) U^(k-1), hence U <= H(Q); the zero case follows from the integral-root height bound.
findings.impact: Proof simplification only. Retains real R >= 1, integer U >= 2R, distinct bounded integer shifts, all even degrees d >= 2, and the exact constant 64. No downstream exponent changes. No error in the original analytic inequalities is asserted.
findings.validation: Full Lean v4.36.0-rc2 build and actual kernel axiom audit for all 545 declarations at the recorded implementation commit.

findings.original_assumption: The combined lemma assumes B comparable to log N and H comparable to B, with fixed comparison constants.
findings.finding: The local bound needs only H=O(B) with B comparable to log N. The global and two-defect-window conclusions need only upper logarithmic bounds on H and window length, without the intermediate B. A lower comparison H comparable to B is unnecessary for all three conclusions, within the paper cutoff domain H >= 2.
findings.proposed_revision: Use H=O(B) for the local estimate, retaining B comparable to log N. State the global count uniformly for H <= D log N and integer counting height X <= CN, and the dyadic two-defect-window count uniformly for H <= D log N and L <= E log N, with fixed constants. All fixed real affine interval changes retain the conclusions.
findings.impact: Strengthens parameter scope in all three parts of T1.3, including fixed bounded cutoffs in the paper domain. No change to exponents 1/2 or 0 and no error in the original conclusion is asserted. The entire T1.3 lemma, including exact affine window geometry, is now proved.
findings.validation: Full Lean v4.36.0-rc2 compilation and actual kernel axiom audit for all 862 declarations at the recorded full implementation commit. Earlier partial validation is retained in validation_history.

validation_history.scope: Global and two-defect conclusions; no lower logarithmic cutoff required.
All three T1.3 conclusions with weaker cutoff hypotheses, literal B=L+1, independent component quantifiers and exact fixed real affine interval versions.

findings.original_assumption: U is comparable to N on both sides and B=O(log N); the general rank conclusion is stated for B asymptotic to c log N.
findings.finding: Only a fixed lower bound U>=aN is needed in every local-rigidity conclusion. For each fixed t and 0<c<2-2^(1-t), one threshold controls all bases U>=aN and all positive lengths B<=c log N. The upper base bound and the asymptotic lower comparison on B are unnecessary.
findings.proposed_revision: Fix a>0 and state local rigidity uniformly for U>=aN. For each fixed t and 0<c<2-2^(1-t), the relation rank is less than t uniformly for all positive B<=c log N. The finite Griesmer bound is uniform in every t after N, whereas t remains fixed before the asymptotic rank threshold.
findings.impact: Strengthens the local-rigidity domain to arbitrarily large bases and every shorter logarithmic window. The constant 64, critical coefficient 1/log 2, sharp rank thresholds and error exponents are unchanged. Actual infinite-model critical-band marginals remain p or 2p and satisfy the proved pointwise (2*2^C)/N bound.

findings.original_assumption: For B≥2, a nonempty even set I⊆[-B,B] with cardinality m, and x>(B+1)^(12m), the translated product is not an integer square.
findings.finding: The stronger threshold x>(64B)^m suffices, hence the simpler uniform threshold x>(B+1)^(5m) for B≥2. It follows directly from the proved degree-uniform algebraic split-product theorem.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace the exponent 12m by 5m, or state the sharper condition x>(64B)^m. Prove the result by the internal T1.1 bound with U=x and R=B; the threshold itself gives x≥2B.
findings.impact: Strengthens the finite local square exclusion. Distinct integer offsets, positive even m and the original domain B≥2 are retained. The original statement and all later exponents remain valid; no optimality of the new threshold is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: The number of 10B-defective positions in every critical window is O_C(B/log B). Companion T9.3 likewise states its free-component error as O_C(B/log B).
findings.finding: One positive absolute multiplicative constant works for every fixed critical-band width C. Only the eventual threshold N0 depends on C. The count is the actual kernel-one set in the full vertex interval. The free-component comparison in T9.3 also has an absolute multiplicative constant before C, with a C-dependent threshold, by the complete rank-cost proof and the critical local-kernel bound.
findings.proposed_revision: There exists an absolute K>0 such that for every fixed C there is N0(C), and all N≥N0(C), all critical-band lengths L and all dyadic starts x, the number of n∈V_x with K_(10B)(n)=1 is at most K B/log B, where B=L+1. In T9.3, the same quantifier order also gives an absolute constant for |c-d_xy|≤K B/log B, with only the threshold depending on C; the multiplicative constant need not equal the one in T9.2.
findings.impact: Clarifies and strengthens the constant uniformity in T9.2. The threshold may still depend on the fixed band width. No admissibility, positive start probability or full-rank assumption is added. The cutoff 10B and the B/log B rate are unchanged. This constant uniformity propagates to the full free-component estimate in T9.3, including overlapping physical windows. The two local kernels are bounded using the proved critical rigidity theorem; no regularity or admissibility premise is introduced.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T22.2 assumes regular windows, hence a common marginal p, and gives q(I)≤p·sum_x q(I\{x}) and the ordered-tuple bound RNp·E(Z_G)_(R-1).
findings.finding: The same missing-full-support condition gives q(I)≤sum_x p_x q(I\{x}) for arbitrary windows with their exact heterogeneous marginals, including incompatible events and zero marginals. If pmax≥0 bounds every actual marginal on G, the tuple sum is at most R|G|pmax·E(Z_G)_(R-1). Regularity is needed only to substitute the nominal p, and |G|≤N yields the original bound.
findings.proposed_revision: State the pointwise missing-block inequality with exact p_x on an arbitrary finite family. State its ordered-tuple consequence with |G| and any nonnegative upper bound pmax for the actual marginals. Then specialize to regular windows, pmax=p=2^(-L), and |G|≤N to recover the original assertion.
findings.impact: Extends the probability and tuple estimates to heterogeneous or irregular windows. It retains affine incompatibility and the exact structural missing-full-support premise. No independence, separation, positive-marginal filter, moment bound or cardinality cutoff is added. The original exponent and constant RNp are unchanged as a corollary.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T9.4 selects a primitive integer factor Q of a nonzero bivariate integer polynomial P, and also bounds its integer quotient.
findings.finding: Primitivity of Q is unnecessary. Every integer factorization P=Q*R with P nonzero gives the same exact bounds for both factors, with constant 2^(dX+dY) and the same sqrt((dX+1)(dY+1)) coefficient rectangle factor.
findings.proposed_revision: For every nonzero P in Z[X,Y] and every integer factorization P=Q R, both H(Q) and H(R) are at most 2^(dX+dY)||P||₂, which is at most 2^(dX+dY)sqrt((dX+1)(dY+1))H(P). Remove the primitive adjective; no separate content adjustment is needed.
findings.impact: Weakens a hypothesis without changing the original constants or partial-degree dependence. The proof uses univariate Mahler bounds and Parseval and includes degree-lowering specializations. The original primitive-factor conclusion is retained. No error in the manuscript conclusion or its multivariate proof is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T23.1 restricts the quadratic-reference parameter to 0≤a≤1 in the exact positive factorial-moment perturbation.
findings.finding: The same epsilon and the same pointwise factors and exact total variation formula hold on 0≤a≤2. The perturbation is nonzero for a<2; at a=2 it vanishes, and all moments agree. The uniform exponential-moment bound on the enlarged interval uses 1+(exp(t)-1)² instead of 1+(exp(t)-1)²/2. The original sharper bound is retained on [0,1].
findings.proposed_revision: State the nontrivial construction for 0≤a<2, and optionally include a=2 as the zero-perturbation endpoint. Keep epsilon, the pointwise 1/2 and 3/2 factors, the factorial-moment difference and the exact TV formula. For a uniform exponential bound on 0≤a≤A≤2, use (3/2)exp(exp(t)-1)(1+(A/2)(exp(t)-1)²); A=1 recovers the original proof bound.
findings.impact: Weakens the parameter restriction without changing the original construction or distance constant. Equality of factorial moments occurs exactly off order m when a<2; the endpoint degeneracy is explicit. The enlarged uniform exponential constant is stated separately. The original range and all its conclusions remain proved. No error in the original statement and no optimality of an obstruction rate are claimed. The subsequent unnumbered m_N/Stirling argument is proved at a later separate checkpoint; the parameter extension alone is not used as a substitute for that proof.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T19.13 assumes mu>0 for the Poisson comparison and 0<mu,nu<=M for stability.
findings.finding: The Poisson comparison holds unchanged for mu>=0, including the actual point-mass reference at mu=0. Stability holds for every real mu and nu with upper bound 2(1+abs(mu))TV(P,Q)+abs(mu-nu). The source bound with M therefore needs only 0<=mu<=M; no positivity or upper bound on nu is needed.
findings.proposed_revision: Include mu=0 in the recurrence-norm/Poisson comparison. State the all-real stability estimate with 2(1+abs(mu)), then specialize to 0<=mu<=M for the original 2(1+M) bound, allowing arbitrary real nu. Retain the original no-first-moment scope.
findings.impact: Weakens only parameter hypotheses. All original constants and conclusions are retained. The reference Poisson law still requires mu>=0; only the recurrence norm and its stability admit negative parameters. Absolute convergence and the factorial resolvent are proved without a first-moment assumption, as already claimed in the source. No error in the original result is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T2.2 assumes natural K,d>=1 and uses the full number n of coordinate positions in its codimension bound.
findings.finding: The bound holds with n_plus, the number of coordinates whose forms are initially nonzero on R, in place of n. The construction and both final regularity properties hold for all natural K and d, including zero, with the same denominators K+1 and d+1 and exact codimension card(D).
findings.proposed_revision: Let n_plus count the initially nonzero coordinate forms with multiplicity and use n_plus/(K+1)+(s-r)/(d+1). Allow K,d>=0. The original statement follows from n_plus<=n; K=0 forces the final space to be zero, while d=0 forbids decompositions of a present nonzero form into two distinct present nonzero forms.
findings.impact: Improves the finite codimension budget when initial coordinate forms vanish and includes the zero boundary parameters. The exact selected-coordinate description, codimension equality, unordered-label convention and simultaneous stopping properties are preserved. There is no claim that arbitrary later restrictions preserve regularity, and no error in the original result is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T2.3 has a three-block partition, at most one coordinate occurrence per block in a row, and gives ternary incidence at most 2*d*K^2 after identifying repeated supports.
findings.finding: The ternary incidence is at most d*K^2. An unordered decomposition of the vertex label chooses two full coordinate-label classes, each of size at most K, so their product already covers both block assignments. More generally no three-block coloring is needed if each row support has size at most three; nonzero labels, zero row sums and the two regularity bounds suffice.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace the sufficient incidence bound 2*d*K^2 by d*K^2. State the row-type and component conclusions for any family of supports of size at most three with zero label sum, after deleting zero labels and identifying repeated supports. The three-block situation is an immediate specialization.
findings.impact: Improves one finite constant and weakens the combinatorial structural hypothesis. Binary component size K, the actual coordinate restriction and the unordered-label convention remain unchanged. The original statement follows and no original conclusion is corrected. No optimality of the new bound or preservation under later restrictions is asserted.
